title: Costs: billing models, budgets and spend alerts

videos.script: A company moves its shop to the cloud. The estimate said three hundred dollars a month. The first bill says five hundred and twenty. {{bill}} Nobody lied, and nothing is broken. The machines cost what they were supposed to cost. The difference is in lines nobody drew. A gateway billed by the hour. Addresses billed whether they are used or not. Traffic leaving for the internet. {{lines}} The cloud does not bill per server. It bills per unit of use, and every decision in this course has a unit and a price. In this lesson you will read those prices on the public list, the way a program reads them. You will estimate a small application line by line, and see which lines catch people out. {{estimate}} Then come the ways to pay less: free tiers, commitments and spare capacity. Each one has a condition, and each condition costs money when it breaks. {{discounts}} Last, the tools that watch the money: budgets, alerts, tags, and the bill read as data. An alert tells you. It does not stop anything. {{watch}} There is no cloud account in this course. Every price is a line of a published list, and every sum is done where you can check it. {{list}}
